Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

consult verb

ask for advice or information

also ask (someone’s) advice, see (a doctor), call in a doctor, look up (in a book)

classical

Cic. Fam. 11.29.1: cum tē cōnsuluissem, quid mihi faciendum esse cēnsērēs (Lewis & Short)
Ov. Ars 3.136: speculum suum (Lewis & Short)

cōnsulō, cōnsulere, cōnsuluī, cōnsultum

verb, third conjugation; + accusative: consult; + dative: look after

consult, ask the advice of

With the accusative, to ask someone’s opinion: a friend, a lawyer, an oracle, even a mirror (Ovid). With the dative it means to look after someone’s interests (sibi cōnsulere), and used alone, to deliberate.

Other words

  • medicum adhibeō, adhibēre, adhibuī, adhibitum — call in a doctor

    also used · classical · Cic. Fat. 12: medicum (Lewis & Short, s.v. adhibeō)

    To bring someone in to help: a doctor, a witness, an adviser.

Examples

  • Sī dolor nōn dēsierit, medicum adhibēbimus.

    If the pain doesn’t stop, we’ll call the doctor in.composed

See also adviser, ask, doctor.

SourcesLewis & Short: consulo · Lewis & Short: adhibeo
